chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Hadeed, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When your skin trembles (with emotion) and your eyes shed tears, then make supplication, make supplication, for your purpose has been aimed at (i.e., your prayer is likely to be answered).
He said, and Muhammad ibn Ismail narrated it from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Muhammad ibn Abu Hamza, from Saeed, similarly.

key_terms.اقْشَعَرَّ: to tremble or stand on end (referring to skin/hairs due to emotion)
key_terms.قُصِدَ: was aimed at / targeted (indicating acceptance of prayer)

ai.seo_question: What are the physical signs that indicate a supplication (dua) is likely to be answered according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the physiological manifestations of khushu’—skin trembling and weeping—as definitive indicators that the supplicant has reached the threshold of divine acceptance. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on the unity of heart, tongue, and body in prayer, suggesting that such visceral reactions signify the removal of barriers between the servant and the Creator. It serves as both a comfort to the supplicant and a benchmark for the sincerity required in du'a.
